result.topic_en: Evaluation of the definite integral of (cos ax − cos bx)/x from 0 to infinity by writing it as a double integral with the factor e^{-tx} and reversing the order of integration, giving log(b/a).
result.transcription:
Math 28
Das bestimmte Integral
$\int_0^\infty \frac{(\cos ax - \cos bx)\,dx}{x} = \omega$
Man betrachte zuerst das doppelte Integral
$\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dt.dx = \Omega$
Die erste Integration nach t gibt indefinite
$\int (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dt = -\frac{\cos ax - \cos bx}{x} e^{-tx}$
also von $t=0$ bis $t=\infty$
$\int (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dt = \frac{\cos ax - \cos bx}{x}$.
Folglich $\Omega = \omega$.

Setzt man
$\Omega = \int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dx.dt$
und bemerkt dass indefinite
$\int \cos ax\, e^{-tx} dx = \frac{a\sin ax - t\cos ax}{aa+tt} e^{-tx}$ wie leicht durch Differentiation bestätigt wird
Folglich indefinite
$\int (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dx = \left\{ \frac{a\sin ax - t\cos ax}{aa+tt} - \frac{b\sin bx - t\cos bx}{bb+tt} \right\} e^{-tx}$
und von $x=0$ bis $x=\infty$
$\int (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dx = \frac{t}{aa+tt} - \frac{t}{bb+tt}$
und mithin
$\Omega = \int_0^\infty \left(\frac{t}{aa+tt} - \frac{t}{bb+tt}\right) dt$ $\neq$
Da nun die indefinite ist
$\int \left(\frac{t}{aa+tt} - \frac{t}{bb+tt}\right) dt = \frac{1}{2}\log\frac{aa+tt}{bb+tt}$
so wird
$\Omega = \frac{1}{2}\log\frac{bb}{aa}$, [-und-] $\omega = \log\frac{b}{a}$ insofern $b$ u. $a$ gleiche Zeichen haben

methods.what: Representing 1/x as the integral of e^{-tx} over t from 0 to infinity to turn a single integral into a double integral
Integration over t of the exponential factor
methods.quote: $\int (\cos ax - \cos bx) e^{-tx} dt = -\frac{\cos ax - \cos bx}{x} e^{-tx}$

methods.what: Antiderivative of cos(ax) e^{-tx}, verified by differentiation
methods.quote: $\int \cos ax\, e^{-tx} dx = \frac{a\sin ax - t\cos ax}{aa+tt} e^{-tx}$

methods.what: Laplace transform of cos ax − cos bx
Interchanging order of integration in the double integral
Frullani-type result: integral of (cos ax − cos bx)/x from 0 to infinity equals log(b/a) when a, b have the same sign
